_: Each entry breaks ONE gate rule in a throwaway clone and names the battery case that must notice. `expect: survives` is a gap written down on purpose, never an oversight - see the reason on the entry. Seeded from a sweep that silenced all 115 report sites in scripts/gates/lib/*.py one at a time; 24 of them survived, and those 24 are the finding, not entries here.

mutants.breaks: the inert-marker filter is applied to the whole LINE instead of to the match, so one `example` in a comment deletes a live-format key sitting beside it
the inert-marker filter never fires, so every documented placeholder is reported as a secret
a GitHub token whose checksum does not validate is reported as a fact rather than as a likely fixture
a GitHub token with a VALID checksum is downgraded to `likely a fixture`, which is the direction that would hide a real leak
mutants.why: covering this branch means committing a string GitHub push protection recognises as a live token to a public repository. That is refused, so the gap is written down instead. If it is ever closed by other means, this gate goes red asking for the bank to be updated.

mutants.find:
findings.append(
            f"the key seals {sealed[:23]}... and {cases_rel} hashes to {digest[:23]}...: the cases "
            "were edited and the key was not, so every answer in it is about a file that no longer exists")
mutants.replace: pass  # mutant: the report above is silenced
mutants.breaks: the eval key stops being resealed when the cases change, so an answer key can drift away from the cases it answers without a word

mutants.replace: pass  # mutant: the report above is silenced
